A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RDIRL, with matching methods, benchmarks, equations, and appendices. All 16 pages of v3 and 17 pages of v5 support comparison. Figure 3 has a clipping defect in v5, but its content remains identifiable.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original continuous-control and cognitive-radar simulation results. Appendix A.5 reports additional online-adaptation comparisons.

after.justification: Section 6 retains original continuous-control and cognitive-radar results. Appendix B.5 reports online-adaptation results, including ML-IRL-online.

M1.justification: The loss formula, regularization, recursive Newton updates, Algorithm 1, and network architectures remain unchanged. Renaming the upper-bound loss as a moment-matching loss does not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CartPole, MountainCarContinuous, HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker2d, and cognitive radar. The appendix streaming comparisons retain CartPole and HalfCheetah; adding a comparator does not expand task coverage.

E2.justification: The batch UB comparator is recast as ML-IRL following the moment-matching interpretation, without a documented procedural distinction. The clear addition is ML-IRL-online in Figure 4 and Table 4. Other comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1 and Figures 1 and 4 switch from raw rewards to expert-normalized reporting, with corresponding changes in Table 4. Walker2d was already normalized. Table 3 retains the training budgets and MPPI settings; rerunning the experiments is not established.

E4.justification: The existing online-adaptation analysis is extended to ML-IRL on CartPole and HalfCheetah. Section 6 also newly reports preliminary failures of competing methods with their original RL inner policies in streaming mode, without detailed supporting measurements.

E5.justification: The 12-run continuous-control and five-run radar protocols remain, alongside shaded curves and tabulated uncertainty. However, v5 removes Section 6.1's explicit identification of the plotted uncertainty as standard deviations, making its meaning less clearly documented.

E6.justification: The control-benchmark results change beyond common rescaling. Table 1 ranks SQIL above RDIRL on Hopper in v3 (257.15 versus 220.79), but RDIRL above SQIL in v5 (0.803 versus 0.799). Online results and curves are revised, and ML-IRL-online entries are added. V5 also gives conflicting RDIRL CartPole uncertainty values in Tables 1 and 4: 0.013 versus 0.13. These changes do not establish comparable-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The upper-bound derivation, Theorem 5.1, and recursive derivation in Appendix A.4/B.4 retain the same mathematics. The moment-matching connection adds interpretation and attribution, without a new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: V3 presents the upper-bound objective and recursive algorithm as two contributions. V5 substantially reframes the former as identifying an existing moment-matching loss as an upper bound, emphasizing the recursive algorithm as its main contribution. The abstract's online-learning and performance claims remain.

C2.justification: V5 adds the moment-matching interpretation and removes the argument that UB's benchmark performance demonstrates bound tightness. It expands the MPPI rationale and streaming applicability discussion, and strengthens the attribution of performance advantages to recursive, adaptive updates.

D1.justification: V5 removes v3's statement that experts start from a fixed initial condition while learners start randomly each epoch. This reduces reproducibility information without establishing changed initialization procedures. Hyperparameters, architectures, hardware, runtimes, and the supplementary-code disclosure are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Swamy et al. (2021) and Zeng et al. (2022, 2025) become central to positioning the objective as existing moment-matching work and distinguishing RDIRL's recursive optimization contribution. This substantially revises attribution and novelty positioning. Haarnoja et al. (2018) also adds SAC context.

P1.justification: The introduction and experimental overview are extensively rewritten around moment matching and batch-versus-streaming comparisons, replacing the earlier two-question UB/RDIRL narrative. Section 4 is retitled, results discussion is condensed, the conclusion is revised, and Appendix A becomes Appendix B.

P2.justification: The four figures and four tables remain, with changed typography, review headers, float placement, normalized axes, and comparator legends. Table 4 gains a row and moves to a separate page. Figure 3's legend and caption are clipped below v5's page 9.

improvement.justification: V5 improves attribution to moment-matching research and adds a relevant streaming comparator. However, normalization accompanies unexplained result revisions, previously consistent CartPole entries acquire conflicting uncertainty values, and Figure 3 loses its visible legend and caption. The PDFs do not clarify the substantive empirical revisions sufficiently to determine whether the gains outweigh these reporting defects.
